\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
The quantity $C=AB$ below is a local equal-time product, not a contour
convolution.  Thus its lesser component is defined locally by
$C^{<}=A^{<}B^{<}$.  The Langreth convolution rule is recalled only for
contrast and does not apply to this local product.  Nevertheless, suppose
one writes
\begin{equation}
C^{<}=A^{r}\,B^{<}+A^{<}\,B^{a}.\label{local-lesser}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
